title: Особый ужин и очередь в туалет  (A Special Dinner and the Restroom Line)

segments.t: Trying to keep his temper in check, Chef Barinov waves away the menus from Ilya and announces that he designed tonight's dinner himself. Vasily excuses himself to find the restroom, where he impatiently insults Nagiyev without realizing he is speaking to the restaurant's owner.
Не все, но умеет.
Не надо меню, спасибо, Илья.
Сегодняшний ужин я придумал сам.
Ну, поделимся.
А мне любопытно, где здесь у вас туалет?
Не так, чтобы знать, нафиг случай.
Вот, пожалуйста.
Просто общительный мальчик.
Дурак, что ли?
Не веришь.
Теперь вы еще и в туалете.
Может, у нас хоть что-нибудь смешное выйдет.
Сейчас, буду я тебя вообще убью, понял?
Let's walk back through the scene line by line.
Не все, но умеет.
'Not everything, perhaps, but she knows how to cook.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'not' before landing on 'knows how'.
Не надо меню, спасибо, Илья.
'We do not need the menu, thank you, Ilya.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'not' before landing on 'Ilya'. Ilya answers right away.
Сегодняшний ужин я придумал сам.
'I designed tonight's dinner menu myself.' The meaning hinges on 'of today's' working together with 'himself' in spoken Russian.
Ну, поделимся.
'Well, we can share.' Max anchors the line on 'come on', while 'to share' completes the thought.
А мне любопытно, где здесь у вас туалет?
'I am curious, where is the restroom in this place?' In Russian, the idea of 'and' flows naturally into 'restroom' without extra filler words. Max answers right away.
Не так, чтобы знать, нафиг случай.
'Not that I need it right now, just in case.' The grammar packs 'not' and 'case' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Вот, пожалуйста.
'Right over there, please.' Notice how Russian expresses 'there you go' and 'there you go' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Просто общительный мальчик.
'He is just a sociable boy.' Max anchors the line on 'just', while 'boy' completes the thought. Ilya answers right away.
Дурак, что ли?
'Are you a fool or what?' In Russian, the idea of 'fool' flows naturally into 'really' without extra filler words.
Не веришь.
'You do not believe me.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'not' before landing on 'do you believe'.
Теперь вы еще и в туалете.
'Now they even have a line at the restroom.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'now' and finishing on 'toilet'. Max answers right away.
Может, у нас хоть что-нибудь смешное выйдет.
'Maybe something funny will finally happen in this place.' The meaning hinges on 'maybe' working together with 'will come out' in spoken Russian.
Сейчас, буду я тебя вообще убью, понял?

'Keep talking and I will flatten you right here, got it?' Ilya anchors the line on 'any minute', while 'understood?' completes the thought. Let's hear the full exchange one more time at natural speed.
